projects.name: Increased resilience of mountain ecosystems, flagship species and communities to climate change through climate-smart conservation and ecosystem-based adaptation
projects.description: A new ecological corridor of around 800,000 hectares, or 8,000 km², has been announced by the Kyrgyz Republic on 22 May 2025. The corridor is set to link up existing conservation areas and complete a protected area spanning a total of over 1,2 million hectares, in a landmark move for biodiversity. As the largest protected area of its kind in the country, it will enable snow leopards and their prey to better adapt to climate change. Also, grazing density will be reduced by almost one quarter, in agreement with local herders, to help restore pastures and allow wildlife to graze. This ecological corridor could become a model for Central Asia. The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) supported the Kyrgyz government by providing ecological modelling to help define the corridor’s borders. The area will connect the Khan-Tengri National Park and Naryn Nature Reserve, passing through several other conservation areas along the way. The corridor aims to safeguard migration and dispersal routes for key mountain wildlife species under pressure from changing habitat conditions due to overgrazing and climate change. Link: https://www.unep.org/news-and-stories/press-release/kyrgyz-republic-unveils-800000-hectare-ecological-corridor

projects.name: Integrated Community-based Management of High Value Mountain Ecosystems in Southern Kyrgyzstan for Multiple Benefits
projects.description: The objective of the project is to secure high value mountain ecosystem biodiversity and associated ecosystem services, while ensuring resilient and sustainable livelihoods in Kyrgyzstan’s Pamir-Alai landscape. The project’s components have been designed to address key threats and corresponding barriers to sustainable land management and biodiversity conservation within mountain forest and pasture ecosystems including Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) found in Kyrgyzstan’s Pamir-Alai Mountain landscape. The project will deliver Global Environmental Benefits using a participatory approach that ensures promotion of women, youth and vulnerable groups and equitable participation opportunities. The project’s approach is closely linked with the Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) conceptual framework, and the project applies the avoid-reduce-reverse principle. The “avoid” principle is applied through the strengthening management of PAs, and improved spatial land use planning. The reduce principle is applied through improved forest and pasture management. The expected project results will be improved management and biodiversity conservation within 6 KBAs that cover 866,000 ha. The project will contribute to the establishment of 4 new national-level PAs covering 281,083.79 ha. Additionally, the project will support the improved management effectiveness of 5 national-level protected areas covering 153,250 ha. The project will improve the management of 563,949 hectares of high conservation value forest (HCVF) lands, including 500 hectares of degraded forest. The project will improve the management of 621,905 hectares of pastures, including 19,500 ha of degraded pastures. The project will improve livelihood benefits for 94,883 people, while improving the conservation status of globally significant biodiversity, and supporting Kyrgyzstan’s progress toward LDN.

projects.name: Climate knowledge of communities and institutions is strengthened to improve their capacity to respond to climate change at local level
projects.description: The headwaters of main river systems in Central Asia heavily depend on the seasonal melting of cryosphere, with little additional precipitation input in their lower reaches. These rivers sustain the lives and livelihoods of the people and the economic development in the region, including Kyrgyzstan. However, glaciers in Kyrgyzstan are experiencing a rapid decline in mass. Changes in glaciers will have significant effects on the large populations of the region. It is therefore necessary to understand the impact of climate change on the cryosphere in the region and Kyrgyzstan, in particular. Activities under this sub-output aim to strengthen climate knowledge of communities and institutions in Kyrgyzstan to improve their capacity to respond to climate change. The sub-output will support evidence-based adaptation measures through scientific assessment of snow, glaciers, permafrost and water availability, while also fostering cooperation with regional and international partners to share knowledge and best practices relevant to Kyrgyzstan’s climate adaptation priorities.

projects.description: A new ecological corridor of around 800,000 hectares, or 8,000 km², has been announced by the Kyrgyz Republic on 22 May 2025. The corridor is set to link up existing conservation areas and complete a protected area spanning a total of over 1,2 million hectares, in a landmark move for biodiversity. As the largest protected area of its kind in the country, it will enable snow leopards and their prey to better adapt to climate change. Also, grazing density will be reduced by almost one quarter, in agreement with local herders, to help restore pastures and allow wildlife to graze. This ecological corridor could become a model for Central Asia. The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) supported the Kyrgyz government by providing ecological modelling to help define the corridor’s borders. The area will connect the Khan-Tengri National Park and Naryn Nature Reserve, passing through several other conservation areas along the way. The corridor aims to safeguard migration and dispersal routes for key mountain wildlife species under pressure from changing habitat conditions due to overgrazing and climate change. projects.name: Strengthening the justice system through provision of essential legal aid services to  refugees, asylum – seekers and stateless persons, improving due process and justice mechanisms, capacitating state authorities
projects.description:
UNHCR’s interventions during the reporting period contributed to strengthening the justice system and improving access to fair and effective legal remedies for refugees, asylum-seekers, and stateless persons in the Kyrgyz Republic. Through the provision of direct legal assistance, capacity development of national institutions, and community-focused awareness activities, UNHCR supported national efforts to advance the rule of law, uphold equality before the law, and prevent discrimination and rights violations affecting vulnerable groups.
UNHCR’s implementing partner delivered legal aid services and legal counselling to 932 refugees and asylum-seekers, ensuring that individuals at risk of rights infringements received timely, professional support to navigate administrative and judicial procedures. These services improved the ability of persons of concern to understand and claim their rights, access documentation, and address barriers linked to their legal status. In cases where individuals faced unjust or incorrect decisions in asylum procedures, UNHCR’s partner represented 121 asylum-seekers in courts to appeal rejections of refugee status. This direct legal representation strengthened procedural fairness and contributed to the integrity of national asylum systems.
To enhance the capacity of justice-sector institutions, UNHCR supported seven training activities for 185 representatives of law enforcement agencies, the General Prosecutor’s Office, national human rights institutions, and the judiciary. These sessions increased institutional understanding of international protection principles, refugee rights, and citizenship-related issues, thereby improving the ability of state authorities to apply standards of due process, prevent discrimination, and ensure equitable treatment of all individuals under their jurisdiction. This work contributes to strengthening the responsiveness, professionalism, and human rights compliance of justice mechanisms.
Complementing these system-level interventions, UNHCR’s implementing partner organized fourteen information and outreach events for refugees and asylum-seekers on their rights, obligations, and procedures necessary for integration. Through these events, community members gained essential knowledge about legal protections, available grievance mechanisms, and pathways to lawful residence and participation in society. This supported their ability to engage confidently and independently with public institutions, reducing vulnerability to exploitation, discrimination, and rights violations.
Together, these actions contributed to strengthening due process guarantees, improving access to justice, and promoting equal treatment before the law. They supported national efforts to eliminate discrimination and violence against women and girls, promote rule-of-law–based governance, and reinforce institutions responsible for protecting and promoting human rights. Through this combination of legal aid, institutional capacity building, and community empowerment, UNHCR helped advance a justice system that is more accessible, accountable, and inclusive for all.

projects.name: Social Media 4 Peace (SM4P) - building resilience to online harmful content—including disinformation and hate speech—while safeguarding freedom of expression and fostering peace through social media
projects.description:
Social Media 4 Peace (SM4P - https://www.unesco.org/en/social-media4peace) is a global initiative implemented by UNESCO to build societies’ resilience to online harmful content—including disinformation and hate speech—while safeguarding freedom of expression and fostering peace through social media.  

In the digital world, harmful online content can deepen social divisions and even trigger offline violence, which is particularly true in conflict-prone and polarised societies. At the same time, efforts to address the harms of online content must respect and protect human rights, in particular freedom of expression and access to information.  SM4P works to strike this balance between addressing the spread and impact of harmful content while protecting freedom of expression. Importantly, the project aims to capture social, cultural, and linguistic nuances of the geographical areas where it operates to develop locally informed strategies that contribute to peace narratives and advance human rights for all.

Since 2021, the project has been implemented in four pilot countries: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Indonesia, and Kenya. In 2025, building on the knowledge and lessons learned in that initial phase, the project has expanded its efforts to Iraq, Kyrgyzstan, and South Africa, bringing its approach to other countries facing similar challenges.

projects.name: Capacity building activities for safeguarding the environment  - mine tailing and water resources
projects.description:
- Mine tailings safety and the prevention of accidental water pollution The main objectives of the subregional workshop are: to strengthen tailings risk governance; to present recent achievements by Central Asian countries in this area, notably since the last subregional workshop on this topic, held in Almaty, Kazakhstan, in 2019; and to exchange experiences, good practices and lessons learned on the prevention of accidental water pollution from tailings at the regional level.

- Development of joint measures to prevent and respond to pollution of the Syr Darya river in emergencies (Phase i): The overall objective is to reduce and prevent pollution of the water resources of the transboundary Syr Darya river. Currently, the project is in Phase 1 of its implementation, which includes understanding disaster risks and identifying potential sources of accidental pollution (the inventory and hazard/risk map of tailings by the riparian countries is the part of this activity), managing disaster risks and strengthening preparedness for an effective response. 

- Addressing technological/industrial accident risks in national strategies and DRR plans of Kyrgyzstan. Kyrgyzstan is supported with enriching its National DRR strategic documents, incl. its action plan with information on technological/industrial accident risk (within the context of the Industrial Accidents Convention, covering chemical installations as well as tailing management facilities (TMFs)), incl. in relation to Natech and transboundary cooperation).  It aims to set the scene for broader joint cooperation with UNDRR, joining forces in the pursuit of common policy objectives through project-related activities in CA. 

- Conducting an annual meeting of the National Policy Dialogue on water, and develop policy packages upon agreement (laws, studies, etc.). The activities will be done in the frame of the project "Regional mechanisms for the low-carbon, climate-resilient transformation of the energy-water-land Nexus in Central Asia".

projects.name: Capacity building activities to strengthen trade facilitation
projects.description:
The objective is to strengthen trade facilitation and electronic business, regulatory cooperation and standardization policies, agricultural quality standards and trade-related economic cooperation for an increased impact on sustainable development in the ECE region and beyond. 
"Undertake a study, through analysis of available information through desk research and in-depth interviews with trade stakeholders. It willl identify trade policy, regulatory and institutional 
limitations that hold back the transition to circularity for selected industries identified by national authorities. The findings of the assessment will be a key input to national and sub-regional workshops and the  formulation of policy roadmaps or action plans. 
they may discriminate on gender and vulnerable groups in society as appropriate. They will be carried out by international experts on trade and circular economy and work in close cooperation with Government experts and other stakeholders including the UN RCOs, other resident UN agencies and development partners.  After the study is drafted, a national workshop will be held to discuss the findings with national stakeholders and develop action-oriented solutions. The goal is to identify priority policy measures regarding technical regulations and trade and innovation as they matter for hotspot sectors (e.g. commodities, agri-food, garment and footwear, construction), which can be tailored to fill the identified gaps. "
projects.outcome: Green economic growth is accelerated through increased equitable entrepreneurship and employment opportunities, including through the sustainable use of natural resources.
